name: China
summary_text: China demands real caution — authoritarian but not criminalising. The most directly visitor-specific finding is airport discrimination: a Thai trans YouTuber was singled out and subjected to discriminatory treatment at a Chinese airport. The most severe documented case is forced psychiatric commitment: a trans woman was held for 97 days and subjected to electroshock "conversion" therapy under family pressure (she won unprecedented compensation), showing the medical/psychiatric system can be weaponized — though this targeted a resident, not a tourist. Under Xi Jinping, the space for LGBTQ+ organising and expression is shrinking: Pride-month social-media and film censorship, a government crackdown on LGBT NGOs (2023), a performance ban on transgender TV icon Jin Xing, and cancellation of a foreign drag queen's tour. There is no criminalisation of trans identity, no bathroom restriction law, and courts can provide some protection, but there are no anti-discrimination protections. China is a regional gender-affirming-care hub, but the parental-consent barrier applies even to adults.

sources.title: Thai transgender YouTuber alleges sexist treatment at Chinese airport | Thaiger
sources.claim_summary: The Thaiger (May 2025): renowned Thai trans YouTuber Nisamanee 'Nut' Lertvorapong accused Chinese immigration officers of sexist, mocking treatment during a family trip - officers laughed at and questioned her at a Chinese airport. Directly relevant to trans travellers' airport experiences in China.
NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying NYT investigation (Dec 2024) covers transgender 'conversion' practices in China.

sources.title: Transgender woman wins record payout in China after electroshock treatment | China | The Guardian
sources.claim_summary: The Guardian (Nov 2024): performance artist Ling'er, 28, won a record payout after being subjected to electroshock 'conversion' treatment - the first time a trans person won such a case in China; she hoped the case would help other LGBTQ+ people protect their rights.

sources.title: China: Social Media, Films Censored Around Pride Month | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch (Jun 2026): 'China: Social Media, Films Censored Around Pride Month' — platforms scrubbed LGBT-related posts and films around Pride month in a renewed censorship wave.

sources.title: Chinese Communist Party continues crackdown on LGBTQ+ people – Radio Free Asia
sources.claim_summary: Radio Free Asia (Jan 2024): the CCP continues a crackdown on LGBTQ+ people as part of a campaign against 'foreign ideologies' - public display of rainbow flags banned, activism 'all but extinct' on the mainland, in contrast to Taiwan's 2019 marriage equality; queer and trans people report growing abuse.

sources.title: Trans People in China Face Barriers to Gender-Affirming Care
sources.claim_summary: Foreign Policy (Jan 2025): 'Trans People in China Face Barriers to Gender-Affirming Care' — gender transition is treated as 'a family affair': surgery requires parental consent and family involvement, and new rules restrict access.

sources.title: China | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): China's approach is 'don't encourage, don't oppose, don't promote', but increasingly restrictive - the Cybersecurity Law enables censorship of LGBTIQ content; in 2025 several gay dating apps were removed from the Apple App Store and prominent queer accounts forced to rebrand or shut down; most advocacy organisations have closed or gone underground; narrow 'family values' pressure intensifies.

sources.title: Some in China fear a wider LGBTQ+ crackdown after transgender dancer Jin Xing’s shows canceled | CNN
sources.claim_summary: CNN (Jan 2025): 'Some in China fear a wider LGBTQ+ crackdown after transgender dancer Jin Xing's shows canceled' — the cancellation of the famous transgender TV personality's tour fuels fears of a broader clampdown.

sources.title: Swiss drag queen faces Chinese repression - SWI swissinfo.ch
sources.claim_summary: Swissinfo: a Swiss drag queen faces Chinese repression - reporting on the treatment of a gender-nonconforming performer in China.

sources.title: China bans same-sex romance from TV screens | CNN
sources.claim_summary: CNN (Mar 2016): 'China bans same-sex romance from TV screens' — broadcast regulator SAPPRFT guidelines bar depictions of 'abnormal sexual behaviour' including same-sex romance.
